title: SSO & Crypto Onboarding: Decision Deck and Acceptance Criteria
creator: Priya Patel
description: PRD + scope log capturing security and compliance requirements for onboarding enterprise customers into Private/VPC deployments. Focus areas: SSO (SAML v2 + OIDC fallback), provisioning (SCIM), RBAC role model and enforcement, comprehensive audit logging with tamper-evidence, and customer-managed keys (AWS KMS CMEK + optional on-prem HSM). This doc records clarifications from legal and security reviews, scope changes requested by pilot customers, trade-offs for time-to-market, and a checklist of artifacts required for sign-off by security, legal, and product ops.
acceptance_criteria: SAML: Support IdP-initiated and SP-initiated SAML 2.0 flows with configurable NameID (email, persistent, transient), signed assertions, and signature/issuer validation documented in Confluence.
OIDC: When customer IdP supports OIDC, system must accept OIDC tokens and map standard claims to RBAC attributes (email, groups, sub).
Provisioning: SCIM 2.0 optional integration; for customers enabling SCIM, create/update/delete provisioning events within 30s of source change for >95% of events during tests.

RBAC: Define and implement a canonical role model (Org Admin, Security Admin, Billing Admin, App Operator, Read-only) with attribute-based group mapping; role evaluation must be enforced at API and Console surfaces with tests covering privilege escalation attempts.

Audit logs: All auth events (login, assertion, token exchange), admin actions (role grants, key rotations, configuration changes), and key-access events must be recorded. Logs must be append-only, tamper-evident, and exportable to customer SIEM (syslog/forwarder) for Private deployments.

KMS: Support Bring-Your-Own-Key (CMEK) via AWS KMS for hosted and Dedicated; Private deployments must support integration with customer HSM vendor X and AWS CloudHSM via documented operational runbooks.
Key lifecycle: Key rotation must be supported with zero-downtime rewrap for active model encryption keys; rollback plan and rotation verification tests must be present in repo.
Evidence: For sign-off, provide test reports, runbook links, and at least one pilot customer who has completed on-prem key import and successful audit ingestion.
Retention and export: Default audit retention is 90 days for hosted but must be configurable up to 7 years for Private; export tools must allow bulk export for legal eDiscovery within 72 hours.

Operational: SSO onboarding automation (metadata ingestion, cert upload, and test-success validation) completion time should be < 2 business days for standard customers and documented for high-touch enterprise flows.
decisions: Adopt SAML 2.0 as baseline for enterprise Private onboarding; OIDC accepted where IdP provides it but not required.
Implement SCIM 2.0 as opt-in to reduce manual provisioning; initial rollout will include manual provisioning runbook for first 3 pilot customers.
KMS approach: staged support. Phase 1: AWS KMS CMEK for cloud; Phase 2: CloudHSM + vendor HSM adapter for on-prem. HSM vendor support will be certified per-customer in Phase 2.
Audit storage: use immutable write-once-backed stores for audit evidence in Private deployments; hosted logs will be stored in WORM-enabled buckets with read-only export endpoints.
RBAC implementation will use centralized policy engine (policy-as-code) to avoid divergence between Console and API enforcement; policies stored in Git with CICD promotion.
Fallback and emergency access: include emergency service account flow with time-limited elevated scope and human approval tracked in audit logs.
open_questions: Legal: Is customer key-escrow acceptable for certain regulated customers or must we always support customer-only custody?
Security: For on-prem HSM integrations, what minimum FIPS/Security certifications do we require for initial sign-off?
Operations: What SLA do we commit to for audit log export and eDiscovery requests for Private customers (48h vs 72h)?
Engineering: Are there performance implications for per-request KMS checks vs caching key material for short windows in high-throughput workloads?
Product: Do we require SCIM as part of standard onboarding for enterprise or keep as premium add-on?
